tagline: Harbor to harbor along the goose-shaped lake.
intro: From New London the byway follows NH 11 west to Georges Mills at the north end of Lake Sunapee and down to Sunapee Harbor, then NH 103 runs southeast past the entrance to Mount Sunapee Resort, a state park, to Newbury at the foot of the lake. Mostly the road keeps to forested hills and fields, and the lake comes in glimpses, best from the car at Georges Mills, Sunapee Harbor, the state park beach and Newbury Harbor.
The whole byway rings the lake in 39 miles. Its Algonquian name means goose water, and the lake is said to be shaped like a goose in flight, its head at the harbor.

moments.title: Sunapee Harbor
moments.text: The harbor sits where the Sugar River leaves the lake, and before the summer trade took over, the town had a factory turning out 110 clothespins a minute.

moments.title: Newbury Harbor
moments.text: At Lake Station the railroad met the steamboats that circled the lake to its villages and grand hotels, and a railroad museum here keeps the story of that era.
